p01.why: A pure specifier must not occur on a friend function.

p02.why: B makes f pure again, so B is abstract and the program must not create the variable b.

p03.why: The target D* drops the const of the operand const B*, and a dynamic_cast must keep every cv-qualifier.

p04.why: override occurs only on the declaration in the class, and here it is on the definition outside the class.

p05.why: A pointer target needs a pointer operand, and b is a class object.

p06.why: B::f is final, so C must not override it, and C::f overrides it because the signature matches (VIRT-1).

p07.why: A call to a function that returns the abstract class A creates an object of A.

p08.why: Y is not derived from X, so Y* is a different return type that is not covariant.

p09.why: A parameter of abstract class type in a function definition creates an object of an abstract class.

p10.why: B::f is deleted and the override D::f is not, and both must be deleted or both not.

p11.why: A member of a union must not be declared virtual.

p12.why: A pure specifier is = 0, and = 1 is not a pure specifier.

p13.why: The target class D is incomplete, and the class in a dynamic_cast target must be complete.

p14.why: A member function template must not be declared virtual.

p15.why: A member of abstract class type creates an object of an abstract class.

p16.why: D::f is marked override, but B::f is not virtual, so D::f overrides nothing.

p17.why: A function marked final must be virtual, and S::f is not.

p18.why: A new expression must not create an object of the abstract class A.

p19.why: A static member function must not have the name and parameters of a virtual function in a base.

p20.why: D is incomplete at the declaration of the override E::get, so D* cannot be a covariant return type.

p21.why: long differs from int and is not a pointer or reference to a class, so the return type is not covariant.

p22.why: A lambda capture by copy of an abstract class object creates an object of the abstract class.

p23.why: The target of a dynamic_cast must be void*, a class pointer, or a class reference, and int* is none of these.

p24.why: An array of the abstract class A creates objects of an abstract class.

p25.why: virtual must not occur on a definition outside its class.

p26.why: A variable of the abstract class A creates an object of an abstract class.

p27.why: A pure specifier must not occur on a function defined in the class.

p28.why: The cast of a plain A to D& fails and throws, and constant evaluation must not evaluate a failed dynamic_cast of a reference.

p29.why: A pure specifier must not occur on a function that is not virtual.

p30.why: The B constructor makes a virtual call to the pure function f, which is undefined, and constant evaluation must not evaluate an undefined operation.

p31.why: D::f has ref-qualifier && and B::f has &, so D::f does not override B::f and must not be marked override.

p32.why: D::f is deleted and the function it overrides is not.

p33.why: The target D is a class type, and a dynamic_cast target must be void*, a class pointer, or a class reference.

p34.why: B is a private base of X, so B is not accessible in D and X* is not covariant with B*.

p35.why: A consteval function must not override a function that is not consteval.

p36.why: B inherits the pure function g with no final overrider, so B is abstract and b must not be created.

p37.why: delete[] destroys an array of D through a B pointer, which is undefined, so constant evaluation must reject it.

p38.why: A() creates a temporary of the abstract class A.

p39.why: A cast that goes to a base needs an accessible base, and A is a private base of D.

p40.why: A return by value of a derived class is not covariant.

p41.why: A member function with an explicit object parameter must not be declared virtual.

p42.why: A cast down from B needs a polymorphic B, and B has no virtual function.

p43.why: The override returns const D*, which adds a cv-qualifier to the target, so the type is not covariant with B*.

p44.why: B::f is final, and D::f overrides it.

p45.why: A is an ambiguous base of R, so R* is not covariant with A*.

p46.why: A function with a deduced return type must not be declared virtual.

p47.why: A function outside a class must not be declared virtual.

p48.why: A cast that goes to a base needs an unambiguous base, and D holds two A subobjects.

p49.why: A return type of abstract class in a function definition creates an object of an abstract class.

p50.why: virtual can only occur on a member function, and x is a data member.

p51.why: A static member function must not be declared virtual.

p52.why: B and C both override f of the shared virtual base A, so D must override f too.

p53.why: D::f(long) has different parameter types from B::f(int), so it overrides nothing and must not be marked override.

p54.why: A member function with an explicit object parameter must not have the name and parameters of a virtual function of a base.
